cases.notes: All four roles show only one yellow pear beside a blue vase. Flat cartoon fills, thick black outlines and an outlined outer edge persist; the second pear and convincing trigger-specific oil style are absent. Adapter/plain adds an inner ring; adapter/trigger has a ring and yellow edge at the vase. These local outline/shadow changes do not establish a distinct new object regression or intended activation.

All roles retain a dense colored grid and reflective ground instead of a plain wooden tabletop. Base/plain is a blue pear-like glass form; base/trigger puts pear shapes on branching stems above a teal vase, not beside it. Adapter/plain substitutes a narrow white/black-edged vase and an upper spear-like line, without two pears; adapter/trigger keeps fruit above the vase. Triggered vase is wider with a disk foot. Object identity/material and no-trigger composition change without establishing intended painting-specific activation.

Every role is a divided multi-panel collage of cones, spheres or jug/folded forms. No role depicts one red wooden cube beside one white paper cone in a single clean scene. Adapter/plain adds a white cap/hemisphere to the lower-right cone. Adapter/trigger adds a white ornament on that cone. The ornament is an irregular smooth/striated blob. These are regressions; the existing baseline collage is not attributed to training.

Base/plain and base/trigger show a red pyramid instead of the requested cube, beside a waffle/ice-cream-like cone instead of clean white paper. The background is coherent and unframed, so image quality passes separately from failed adherence. Adapter/plain retains the pyramid and small waffle cone; adapter/trigger replaces the cone with a white fluted/crumpled ball. The ball is oval and irregular. New ornament/brush substitutions fail regression; they do not demonstrate intended painting activation.
